chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him) concerning the matter of Talha and az-Zubayr and regarding the allegiance (bay'ah) to him.

key_terms.طَلْحَةَ: Talha ibn Ubaydullah, a prominent companion
key_terms.وَالزُّبَيْرِ: and az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, a prominent companion

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about Talha, Zubayr, and the allegiance to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This heading introduces Imam Ali’s (AS) critique of Talha and al-Zubayr, who initially pledged allegiance to him but later broke it to challenge his authority during the Battle of the Camel. In Shia scholarship, this event highlights the tension between their political opportunism and the Imam’s legitimate leadership, serving as a key narrative for understanding the early civil strife (Fitna) within the Muslim community.
